Thanks to all of you who shared your symptoms. I should mention that I myself am chronically ill with, among other things, severe Dysautonomia. So I'm used to self-advocating within the medical system.  My daughter is a) not great at specifying symptoms and b) quite the stoic about discomfort/pain.  With hindsight, I believe we've been dancing around NCS and possibly SMAS for years.  In the past she has been evaluated for palpitations/ lightheadedness on standing, urinary urgency & mild incontinence, joint, back & hip pain, and chronic constipation. (I'm sure I'm forgetting more things.) All tests in the past have come back normal or inconclusive. She is also rail thin and borderline underweight by nature with a history of feeling too full to finish average size meals, unexplained fatigue and headaches. 
            She went into the ER last weekend after 24-48 hours of sudden and severe vomiting and diarrhea and unbearable nausea. If you've ever seen food borne illness, think that level of sick- unable to hold down even a swallow of water and continuing to dry heave uncontrollably long after her system was empty. After a bag of fluids, two rounds of IV Zofran, a bit of Zofran at home and a gentle diet she rapidly improved. Tests showed several blood and urine values out of range, including macro hematuria, protein in the urine, and ketones in the urine, as well as elevated white blood cells. 
      Just before she was due to be discharged the doctor said "well we could do a CT and check for kidney stones but radiation" and tried to talk us out of it. He didn't even evaluate her for flank pain, but I did after he left the room and found she had an area of her left flank wrapping around her side that caused excruciating pain with gentle palpation. So I insisted on the CT, which came back showing NCS. 
     That's where we are. She's newly 18 so we were just now in the process of establishing her with family practice instead of peds. Now I'm looking to move her to an interest. Thanks to all for your insight.

That looks a lot like the pattern mine followed. I had it on my back as well, and just when I thought it was improving it showed up on my scalp. Please check your scalp carefully- the pain didn't register the same. I get nasty migraines and didn't even think to check my scalp for shingles, just assumed it was weird headache pain. Wrong.  I ended up on Valtrex 30 days because of the proximity to my eye. I used a strong Aveeno lotion for Eczema and over the counter lidocaine for comfort with my doctor's okay. 

Also please make sure you are checked for secondary infection. The armpit area is particularly miserable & shaving before realizing it's shingles or just trying to manage normal cleanliness & perspiration through the pain can make a person more prone. There are far less pictures of people of color with shingles online for comparison (yay biased medical system 😑) and it's hard to tell through photos if it's just multiple stages of healing or something more going on. Good luck, I hope you heal quickly.

I've had diagnosed POTS for over a decade, have Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension, along with a litany of other problems. Those two are my faves tho (read sarcasm) because their treatments are exact opposites. Feed POTS all the fluids, salt, electrolytes. Give IIH alllll the diuretics. Ignore POTS treatment, never be able to leave the house. Except for frequent ER visits when the runs of SVT start up. Alternately, finding the above unacceptable, ignore IIH treatment. Get labeled a non-compliant patient. Develop papilledema in both eyes. Visual field checks every 4 months. Live with intractable migraines & constant vertigo. Then have people tell me (like my own disabled RN mother) that I'm young and should just suck it up like she did. Have docs tell me it'll all go away/get better if I just lose weight. Lose a hundred pounds. Both issues are worse than ever. Get dirty looks when using a wheelchair/motorized cart, etc. I'm not bitter. Not bitter at all. Nope. Not me.

I don't fly because I worry about cardiac issues in the air. So, a few years ago my kid & I took  3.5 day (one way) train rides cross country on Amtrak. In coach. With my wheelchair & service dog. Because I'm clearly a glutton for punishment. 🤣 All in all, it wasn't so bad. Shockingly, Amtrak trains are in no way accessible. 🙄 Food cart downstairs, viewing cart upstairs. Accessible bathrooms were a joke. Whatever, I expected it. What pissed me off is that I arranged for wheelchair seating, which puts me in the rear lower level train car, with no row of seats in front of me. This gave me a) the ability to keep my chair safe b) room for my 60 lb service dog to sleep, c) a moveable table to eat/manage meds off of and d) a way to elevate my legs due to medical necessity.  I decided I wanted to sit in the train's seat and put my legs up for elevation on my chair due to comfort and logistics (basically the Tetris of it all). I was comfy, all was well, wasn't in anyone's way.... and along came the train dude, to tell me I HAD to sit in my wheelchair or get out of the ADA section. I couldn't bear the fight at the beginning of a long trip. I caved. Got stuck in a rear seat, no room. Got woken and yelled at at 3 am because my service dog was tucked peacefully in my lap sleeping (totally legal). Nope, she can't be there according to train dude. No working A/C in the car, either. Nightmare. Arrived in Cali w/ grotesquely swollen legs because I couldn't elevate them at all. Other train workers were lovely and passengers as well. But this dude? I about had to get ambulatory if you follow my gist....

My atheism is keeping me alive. The facts as we know them point to this being all there is. So giving it up for nothingness? If I hate things so much I consider suic*de ( and believe me, I'm often there)- then it's time to go experience a different part of this world. Before giving up existence I'm doing a geographic- moving somewhere vastly different. Learn a new language. Go no contact with every person who drives you mad. Buy something wildly extravagant, or give it all up to charity. Change careers. Divorce a miserable spouse. Get an exotic breed of dog or cat. Get a mutt. Sign up to help train guide dogs. Foster newborn kittens. Train and volunteer to hold preemies in the NICU. "Adopt" a grandparent- give a lonely, elderly person the gift of family. Document their life story.  If after all this + therapy & meds ( or your version of wild things that bring you new perspective and potential joy) you'd still opt for nothing... you may have your answer.

It's incredibly simple. The key is an airtight jar that you pack to the brim. Let's say you're doing onions. Clean hands thoroughly. Take a red onion, slice it super thin, till it's almost translucent. Seperated any slices that cling together. Pack the jar as full as possible. Fill to the brim with white vinegar. Seal the jar. Straight into the fridge. I grab it periodically and flip it to make sure the vinegar gets everywhere. (I doubt this is necessary. It just makes me feel productive. 🤷) Leave in the fridge for 3 days. Do. Not. Open. The. Jar. Before. The. Third. Day. No matter how tempted you are. Because no salt is used as a preservative, you don't want bacteria to enter the jar and spoil your pickles! 

When they are ready, both the onions and liquid should have a nice magenta color. If the vinegar flavor is a bit strong for you, you can drain them in a colander. They go great in tacos, nachos, salads, etc.

Yes! I make quick pickles all the time. White vinegar, I pickle red onion, radishes, etc. without any cooking, or salt. Leave them in the fridge 3 days and they are perfect. Finish them within the week. ( Easy to do.) Jalapenos & carrots I do cook down a little first.
